text:
Anya: quick share — finished M2-mid bring-up + quant sweep. TL;DR: int4 reduces inference cost ~2.4x but we see a regression on long-form QA / multi-turn summarization. short answers look fine.
Jordan: can you post the microbench + eval numbers?
Anya: sure — paste below. concise table, numbers are medians across 5 runs: 
```
model        | config     | cost_per_1M_tokens | p50_latency_ms | p95_latency_ms | QA_EM_delta | Summ_R1_delta
M2-mid       | fp16       | $120               | 82             | 210            | 0.0         | 0.0
M2-mid       | int8       | $72                | 78             | 205            | -0.4        | -0.3
M2-mid       | int4       | $50                | 77             | 220            | -2.3        | -4.6
M2-large     | fp16       | $240               | 140            | 360            | +0.9        | +1.8
```
Notes: cost is infra-only (GPU+infra), not including infra overhead or network. QA_EM_delta relative to fp16 M2-mid baseline. Summ_R1_delta = Recall-1 on our summarization set.
Benchbot: microbench logs attached (shortened): 
```
[benchbot] run 1: int4 throughput 3.2k tok/s, avg mem 6.1G, kv-hit ratio 0.28
[benchbot] run 2: int4 throughput 3.1k tok/s, int8 4.4k tok/s, fp16 4.6k tok/s
```
Rachel: the -2.3 EM on long QA worries product. which slice? long-context >512?
Anya: yes most regressions concentrated on >512 token contexts and multi-step reasoning prompts. short QA (<128) EM delta ~-0.2.
Sam: two immediate levers: 1) hybrid routing by request length, 2) prefix-KV warm cache + partial-fp16 for final decode. hybrid seems simplest.
Priya: from product POV — what's user-visible impact if we do hybrid routing 90/10 (small/int4 for <128)? can we simulate weighted quality score?
Anya: quick simulated weighted quality delta if we route <128 -> int4 (40% traffic), >=128 -> fp16 (60%): weighted_QA_delta ~= (-0.2 * 0.4) + (0.0 * 0.6) = -0.08 EM. Weighted_cost ~= (0.4*$50 + 0.6*$120) ~= $86 per 1M tokens (~28% cost reduction vs all-fp16).
Jordan: nice — latency? p95 will mostly be from the larger bucket so overall p95 ~ between 210-260ms. p50 drops a bit because lots are fast.
Rachel: OK that seems acceptable if product approves. What about safety / hallucination risk with int4?
Anya: hallucination spike small in our evals but we have two mitigations: per-request evaluation hooks (answer-confidence) and fallback: if confidence < 0.55 -> re-run on fp16 variant. fallback increases cost for those requests only. In simulation fallback hit rate ~6% leading to final cost ~$92 per 1M tokens.
Sam: implementation sketch for routing policy (pseudo-config):
```
{"routing": [{"if": "tokens<=128","model":"M2-mid-int4","fallback":"M2-mid-fp16","canary":0.05},
{"if": "tokens>128","model":"M2-mid-fp16","canary":0.05}]
}
```
Anya: rollout plan proposal:
- canary 1% traffic for 24h -> monitor QA EM on live evalset, latency p95, hallucination rate.
- expand to 10% if no regressions beyond threshold (QA EM drop >0.5 on key slices)
- 30% next day, full roll at 72h.
Jordan: add alert if fallback rate >12% or latency p95 increases >30%.
Rachel: product asks for per-customer opt-out and explanatory notes for GTN. also want an A/B with revenue signals for 2 weeks.
Priya: set the acceptance gates: 
- weighted_QA_delta > -0.5 EM across prioritized customers
- fallback_rate < 10%
- infra_cost_savings >= 20%
Anya: final recommendation: go hybrid routing as default for initial bring-up (route short-form -> int4, long-form -> fp16), enable fallback by confidence and 1% canary with strict alerts. Run 2 week A/B for GTN and measure key product metrics. paperwork: I'll open rollout doc and add the bench dumps + eval slices.
Rachel: 👍 please include the eval prompts and the top 20 failure examples.
Anya: will do, uploading in #eng-ml drive. thanks team. :rocket:
